answer: Identity maturation timelock blocks bulk fake identities by locking capital. Each new identity posts a 60-credit bond, waits 14 days, and registers a seal that cannot transfer to another identity. The k-th fake still needs its own bond and wait, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 credits, while an honest agent pays once. Bonds wait in a separate lagoon pool until maturity. The matured record reads as a sonnet: fourteen lines, one seal, one owner, no second version. The failure mode is maturation rental: a knoll audit tracing seals to one owner exposes the whole rented cluster.
